name: Blockwise Parallel Transformer for Large Context Models
problem: Self-attention memory and the feedforward layer's activation memory both limit the sequence length a single device can train on, so long-sequence tasks need awkward chunking or approximations.
mechanism: Blockwise computation of self-attention combined with FUSION of the feedforward network into the attention block, so the activation memory for both is bounded by one block rather than by the full sequence. Attention within a block is computed exactly; the block decomposition changes memory, not the attention arithmetic. This is the single-device work whose device-level distribution became Ring Attention.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): enables training sequences 32x LONGER than vanilla Transformers and up to 4x longer than previous memory-efficient methods. This is a CAPACITY claim (max trainable sequence length), not a throughput or latency speedup - the mechanism reduces memory, and the number expresses how much sequence that buys. Quoting '32x' as a speedup would misstate it.
